chunks: And al-Riḍā, peace be upon him, said:
"Every path that is trodden and used as a thoroughfare, whether there is a main road in it or not, salat (prayer) should not be performed in it."
It was said, "Then where should one pray?" He said, "To the right or to the left."

key_terms.طَرِيقٍ: a path or roadway used for passage
key_terms.يُتَطَرَّقُ: used as a route of travel or passage

ai.seo_question: Can salat (prayer) be performed on a commonly used path or roadway?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that salat (prayer) should not be performed in a path that people tread and commonly use for passage. Instead, one should move to the side of the path, preserving both the propriety of worship and the right of passage for others.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.728 - Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha (as) said:
"Any path that is trodden and commonly used, whether it has a main road or not, should not be used for prayer."

He was asked: "Then where should one pray?"
Imam (as) said: "To the right or to the left (of the path)."
